display.title: Mitzvah Time: Why We Smell Spices at Havdalah
display.summary_short: Why we smell besamim at Havdalah when the extra Shabbos soul departs, why Havdalah opens with words of trust, and how counting the days toward Shabbos and keeping it can bring Moshiach.
display.summary_long: A Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, continuing the laws of Havdalah. After reviewing the Havdalah kit, Uncle Yossi explains that when Shabbos arrives Hashem gives us an extra soul, the neshamah yeseirah, which makes us feel happy and holy, so we daven, learn and behave better. When Shabbos ends it returns to Hashem and we feel a little sad, so we smell sweet spices and bless Hashem for them to lift our spirits. Hashem reassures us that He stays with us all week, which is why Havdalah opens with 'Behold, G-d is my salvation, I will trust and not fear', and he recalls the Baal Shem Tov's father telling him to fear nothing but Hashem. Shabbos is the day Hashem Himself rested; we count the days toward it in the daily Song of the Day, as we counted toward Shavuos, and save good food and new clothes in its honor. The Gemara says that if all Jews kept Shabbos properly, Moshiach would come immediately.
display.lesson: Shabbos is so holy that we long for it all week; keeping it properly can bring Moshiach, and we start every week trusting Hashem.
